questions.scenario: A support app answers "What are your store hours?" thousands of times a day. The answer is in a table.
questions.question: How should the request be handled?

options.why: The data is a simple lookup.

options.text: By a rules engine that reads the table, with no model call
options.why: Correct. Code answers exactly and for free.

questions.explanation: Use rules when code can decide exactly.

questions.scenario: The app must label 100,000 reviews as positive, neutral or negative every hour at low cost.
questions.question: Which component fits?

options.text: A large reasoning model for every review
options.why: It is more costly than needed.
Correct. It is cheap and fast for simple labelling.

questions.explanation: Send simple, high-volume work to small models.

questions.scenario: A team wants a service to choose a suitable model for each prompt automatically.
questions.question: Which feature fits?

options.why: Correct. It selects among underlying models per prompt.

questions.explanation: A model router is one way to send prompts to different models.

questions.scenario: A hybrid design uses rules, a small model and a large model.
questions.question: In what order should a request be tried to reduce cost?

options.text: All three in parallel for every request
Rules first, then the small model, then the large model only when needed
options.why: Correct. The cheapest adequate component handles each request.

options.text: Large model first, then the small model
options.why: Every request would pay the highest price.

options.text: Small model first for every request, including exact lookups
options.why: Rules answer exact lookups more cheaply and reliably.

questions.explanation: Cascade from cheapest to most capable.

questions.scenario: The small model returns a low-confidence label for some reviews.
questions.question: What should the design do?

options.text: Escalate those requests to a larger model
options.why: Correct. A fallback improves quality for hard cases.

questions.explanation: Escalation keeps cost low while protecting quality.
